The two paid-chain contractions in this PR, paired with a 480-factor BIT supplier, give **conditional κ ≥ 0.00387992803556**. The five inherited premises are `native_all_columns`, `owned_erasure`, `compiler`, `precision_tape`, and `analytic_recovery`. The first paid factor determines the cutoff. Grades 1 through 4 use `10^480` and higher grades use `11^480`. Reordering the same factors gives a concrete paid tuple that takes two calls in one order and one in the other. Compared with #7835, the construction reduces the tensor from 832 factors to 480 and the required log₂ N by 21.8%. The complete application charges 36 BIT calls and 48 rational calls at the original signed prices. The independent replay reproduced the complete rational application and audit byte for byte and checked 54 strict and four functional outer conditions. pull_requests.title: Prove the all-column native operators of the complete grade-14 multiplier
pull_requests.body:
This proof removes `native_all_columns` from the complete grade-14 multiplication claim. For arbitrary binary operands of at most n bits, the fixed-tape time remains O(n (log n)^(1−κ)) at **κ = 0.00387992802601**. The original application needed five premises. This construction needs four. The limiting outer cost remains the main transform. [Operator proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a7f99a5f5f919dd3ffb2987f90c1e7d6527feb1e/research/grade14-native-realization/PROOF.md) · [Physical routes and leaves](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a7f99a5f5f919dd3ffb2987f90c1e7d6527feb1e/research/grade14-native-realization/ROUTES.md) · [Complete application](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a7f99a5f5f919dd3ffb2987f90c1e7d6527feb1e/research/grade14-native-realization/APPLICATION.md) · [Exact receipts](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a7f99a5f5f919dd3ffb2987f90c1e7d6527feb1e/research/grade14-native-realization/RESULT.json)

The eliminated premise required the actual operators, all phases, spectators and whole-job adapters to work at every positive column multiplicity. The native one-column replays and grade counts did not prove that implication. This proof starts at the two words consumed by [PR #7835](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7835), follows arbitrary independent inputs through both recursive boundaries and supplies its imported ordinary interchange rate from elementary operations. [Original five statements](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57/certificates/frontier7000/CLAIM.json) · [Exact word, phase and price inputs](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a7f99a5f5f919dd3ffb2987f90c1e7d6527feb1e/research/grade14-native-realization/ORIGINS.json)

| Interface | Construction and verification |
| --- | --- |
| Complex | Regenerate 2,955 relative Clifford jobs and 208 absolute-phase boundary monomials. Check all 1,289² rational transfer coefficients in each direction. Lift the native chart changes across columns, while retaining each caller coefficient once. This realizes all 48 calls and 30,000 global normalizers at their existing prices. |
| Binary | Use each actual port's head line in the 134-axis caller. Lower the complete low/high cover permutation, its rational carry, the matched donor and inverse return, and both good and nonunit weighted leaves. All 36 calls yield the original 20,706 productive outputs and 107,460 paid positions. |
| Ordinary input and integer output | The elementary digit exchange funds one preparatory grade-14 stage. Its envelope 0.003864408313999584 exceeds the required seed 0.00385248. The four original priced stages then deliver 0.003879928026095. Both supplier rates and all nine outer cost rows support the original κ. |

**Remaining dependencies.** The four original premises are `owned_erasure` for private streams and suspended owners, `compiler` for finite chronological compilation and uniform closure, `precision_tape` for the fixed-tape movement, storage and precision prescriptions, and `analytic_recovery` for the outer decomposition, prime avoidance and exact recovery. They keep their original statements. The proof is specific to the grade-14 application and the words and weights it actually uses. The conservative constants are enormous. We did not materialize either full uniform template or execute an asymptotic-size integer product. Independent human and formal verification of the universal proof remain open. [Qualification and comparison with higher advertised rates](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a7f99a5f5f919dd3ffb2987f90c1e7d6527feb1e/research/grade14-native-realization/VALIDATION.md)

**Verification.** CPython 3.12, standard library only. Run from the repository root.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/grade14-native-realization
```

The five scientific checks emit these markers.

```text
PASS_GRADE14_ALL_COLUMN_COMPLEX
PASS_GRADE14_ALL_COLUMN_BIT
PASS_GRADE14_COMPLETE_LOCAL_RING
PASS_GRADE14_FOUR_PREMISE_APPLICATION
PASS_NATIVE_ATLAS_BUILD c7173d46c95d1311b8b18a92c874fb7013c6e694aa8e9c0c256f0f1eaf1ede74
```

pull_requests.title: Selected native realization under four retained assumptions, with route audit
pull_requests.body:
## Selected κ = 0.00363005817 under four unchanged retained assumptions

This PR combines a separately reviewed complete-cover route lemma with its **exact selected #7000/#7001 native realization**. It establishes the required selected `native_all_columns` instance—phases, spectators, whole-job adapters and a noncircular ordinary seed—*conditional on precisely the other four original contracts*. The canonical selected five-assumption certificate is unchanged. This is a source-specific mathematical reduction, **not** unconditional multiplication and **not** a larger κ.

### Source-specific native realization

The selected binary word is bound to its own 636 rational frames, 2,374 MOVE pairs and 111 paired chart routes rather than importing the larger grade-14 helper inventory or price from #7837. A reverse-functional checker verifies the 38-role BIT caller; the source predicate replay covers 434,281 BIT and 2,190,400 complex scalar coefficient positions. The unchanged application replay checks all 14,400 phase contacts, both paid-owner lists and negative controls. The complete signed-Pauli/Clifford catalogue comprises 3,057 maps plus 104 absolute-phase boundary pairs, freshly replayed with identical logs.

The proof supplies full-ring good-leaf normalization, explicit bad-leaf fallback, complete fresh-cover right routes and inversion, equal route matching for coupled X/Y roles, common ancestor weights, entire tensor/spectator semantics and correct once-only scalar/LAMBDA actions. The recursive implementation strictly decreases width; its ordinary service is bootstrapped from **elementary complete digit exchange**, not assumed from itself. Exact cold-stage targets are `0 -> 0.0034 -> 0.0038507 -> 0.00385248`; their envelope and the selected required saving have strict rational margins. New N-dependent route expansion costs are included in finite template constants, not claimed free.

### Independent route audit and precision challenge

The companion review of #7837 proves the full low/high carry cocycle, inverse return and coupled-role donor criterion. It independently factors all 111 port matchers at q=3 and 5 (222 rational checks), enumerates complete GL₂(Z/3) and GL₂(Z/9), and checks 109,536 common-weight columns plus another 109,536 nonconstant route-invariant-weight cases. Six mutation controls reject missing carry, wrong return/order, route mismatch and noninvariant weights. The algebraic weakening from ancestor-only weights to route-invariant weights does *not* claim a new physical tariff or source descriptor.

A separate selected binary reviewer uses reverse functionals and explicit exponents rather than the author's forward checker. A separate complex reviewer checks **all stored and intermediate scalar preproducts** across 71,261 events, so intermediate division is not inferred only from final endpoints. The retained A=178, B=161, c=356 and W+26 budgets remain sufficient, with controls rejecting wrong phases, tensor-powered exterior scalars and premature unscaling.

### Reproduce / integrity

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/grade14-weighted-route-cross-review
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-native-four-premise-specialization
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/selected-native-four-premise-specialization --check-source-history --check-modes
```

The selected package passed all seven registered commands in both author and separate root replays. Its 101-file tested tree, 60 authenticated scientific source extracts and strict source-history gate were checked on the remote commit. The grouped branch keeps both reviewed package trees unchanged and includes their original commits in Git history.

### Exactly what remains

`owned_erasure`: full blank grants, nonzero erasure, suspended owners and higher callers. `compiler`: all-size mixed-target chronological construction and funding. `precision_tape`: real coded-field movement, layout and retained backing tariffs. `analytic_recovery`: full decomposition, fine-prime transfer, coefficient production and exact integer recovery. **No selected assumption beyond the native instance is claimed discharged.**

Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance; this is not human peer review or proof-kernel verification.

pull_requests.title: Close ordinary BIT interchange under heterogeneous recursive cycles
pull_requests.body:
This construction lets one fixed ordinary BIT program serve both the public entry and all smaller ordinary calls of a funded word through a **cover-free block splitter**. The splitter can earn zero coarse saving. Inserting a bounded chain of such entries preserves the funded characteristic up to a fixed logarithmic power, and preserves every strictly funded pure exponent. One program and one cutoff serve those prices for a fixed compiled word. [Proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f927ed7ffbb2b8870f109d59ddd94e1f87becb13/research/self-hosted-ordinary-interchange/PROOF.md) · [Complete caller and costs](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f927ed7ffbb2b8870f109d59ddd94e1f87becb13/research/self-hosted-ordinary-interchange/APPLICATION.md) · [Implementation](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f927ed7ffbb2b8870f109d59ddd94e1f87becb13/research/self-hosted-ordinary-interchange/interchange.py) · [Exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/f927ed7ffbb2b8870f109d59ddd94e1f87becb13/research/self-hosted-ordinary-interchange/RESULT.json)

**Actual producer and consumer.** Split each of two address fields into halves. Send both corresponding block swaps to the pending four-return word and route every smaller ordinary call from that word back through the splitter. Every request carries the full arbitrary payload, including the odd last block. The splitter borrows no cover row. Its companion pays for the native cover, both reversed bodies, weighted leaves, bad classes and restoration. The elementary digit base supplies all terminal moves.

| Public BIT service | Funded ordinary saving | What it supplies |
|---|---:|---|
| Two-block entry with the pending primary compiler | 0.003879927836154 | The pending multiplier's full original ordinary price of 0.003879927836145 |
| Two-block entry with the independent lower certificate | 0.003879907846154 | Its full independently certified covered price |
| Selected paired word as entry to the asymmetric cycle | ≥ 0.003879632977211447 | The stronger pending multiplier's tested price of 0.00387944011075 |

The original selected word on its own fails that stronger test under its signed tariff. All three public entries have a complete consumer. The pending rational proposal still gives **κ = 0.00387944011068** under the five source assumptions. The rational invoice still fails its higher enrolled target. [Selected review](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57/docs/research/pr-intake-evidence/pr7000-application/PROOF-REVIEW.md) · [Pending rational application](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/blob/89a67c404226d51028e135de2b9169e9020d57af/research/p104-iterated-returns/continuation/evidence/application.json) · [Pending primary finite certificate](https://github.com/Clear1nsight/integer-mult-bounds/blob/89a67c404226d51028e135de2b9169e9020d57af/research/p104-iterated-returns/binary/FINITE.json)

**Why the recursion closes.** A smaller field can still carry the entire input. Splitting a genuine spectator gives each live child at most half the parent's volume. The ordered returns preserve every bit and independent productive output. A block splitter can use widths proportional to its input. Only the funded part has to contract the logarithm of the width. Charging the splitters before solving the recurrence preserves the exponent and linear visited backing. The asymmetric variant also requires revised global stock and outer movement bounds.

**Comparison and limits.** A repriced finite stack of four stages already reaches the primary numerical price. The new capability is arbitrary-width, mutually callable block entries that preserve the complete funded service, including each strict price of a fixed companion. Ordinary prices here are asymptotic. The asymmetric selected entry needs log₂(e) > 59,326,000,000,000,000 when its cover is active. The two-block example keeps the pending stock exponent of 1/250. The source assumptions remain `native_all_columns`, `owned_erasure`, `compiler`, `precision_tape` and `analytic_recovery`. Independent scientific acceptance remains open.

**Sources and credit.** @CubeJerry supplied the selected words. @Clear1nsight supplied the four-return successor, both binary receipts and the original complete consumer. The application retains the earlier dual-supplier gate. @rohanarun supplied the finite bootstrap, @jmbarrancoml the physical ordinary sites, and @mason-hale the segment allocation. Ali Romman (@aliromman) prepared this contribution with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. other_new_prs.body:
## What this PR supplies

This PR combines two directly dependent, individually reviewed results into a single interface contribution: **fixed Gaussian-rational scalars in recursive all-column C words**, followed by a **phase-preserving translation of the selected complex compiler** into that expanded grammar. This closes a concrete mismatch between #7828's odd rational scalars and #7834's dyadic-only receiver without increasing the paid C-call count. It is not a complete physical runtime or a new multiplication bound.

### Exact rational all-column grammar and common grid

Extend the C-word scalar alphabet by `SCALE(a,b,q): z -> ((a+i b)/q)z`, with fixed integers and positive q. The exact matrix-dictionary/Vandermonde test distinguishes scalar multiplication from columnwise phase `i^f`; it checks every productive output and requires all private outputs to be zero. For a word with base rank N and J instructions, let D be the LCM of the odd denominator parts, d=floor(log_N h). One root scale `D^(Jd)` pays all intermediate odd debt, since completed children return dyadic maps and only unfinished ancestor contexts accumulate division debt. A separate coefficient-dependent binary guard pays numerator staging, magnitude and exact final unscaling.

Under the source's named disjoint-XOR, placement, scalar-service and parking contracts, local scalar events cost O_word(V), root scaling costs O_word(V log(h+2)) and the working component width remains O_word(p) in the source geometry. The retained W^d genuine-row stock, <2 padding, zero-output checks, physical history and fallback are not hidden. The proof corrects the unary denominator budget to D≤3^(L/3), avoiding an earlier overstatement.

### Exact selected complex compiler admission

The translation preserves **N, W and the full paid count P** from the selected #7828 complex construction. It lowers each monomial to x/s/cz/cx/unit with signed phases and correct chronological order, retains both source L/R factors and all spectators, handles absolute phase by `i^(a*c*f)`, and applies exterior rational scalars once rather than tensoring them. The selected global LAMBDA is one complete two-term exterior scalar combination. Private SWAP/CLEAR operations are explicitly lowered and charged.

The selected conditional supplier funding check remains `P^500 < W^500 N^499`, with exact source saving `181502908503/50000000000000 > 1/500`. This *supplier price* is not a new complete multiplication κ. The compiled test fixture has 1,654 instructions, 18 paid calls and 28 private fields; it is deliberately unfunded.

### Reproduce

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/rational-all-column-c-word

```

Checks include exact Fraction-array/tensor oracles, deep odd divisions, multiple multiplicities and spectators; the compiler package checks 700 monomial packets, 712,754 exact address/phase comparisons, all 3,095 compact caller events, independent receiver replay and mutation controls for phases, aliases, dirty private exits and wrong exterior-scalar semantics. Both packages retain complete original proofs, source hashes, reviews and registered receipts.

### Boundaries and credit

other_new_prs.body:
## What this PR establishes

This PR groups three sequential, independently reviewed source lemmas rather than opening three overlapping PRs. It upgrades the selected *three-axis* physical Gaussian source from exact nonvanishing to explicit, error-tolerant Stein displacement bounds. The physical chirp/phase coefficients are retained throughout. **No multiplication exponent or foundational-assumption status changes.**

### Exact rank on the actual distinct-prime source

For three extremal two-point fine-prime factors, every one of the **40,320 simultaneous vertex orders** of the 8×8 tensor has ordinary Stein displacement rank eight, as does the exact tensor inverse. This strengthens the general source rank-six floor of CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#7598. A crucial counterexample prevents overgeneralization: three *repeated* factors can have rank six even strictly inside the older positive-decay parameter box. Distinct-prime source structure, not a generic box argument, supplies the positive theorem.

### Quantitative margins and errors

- **Two specified orders:** with common dyadic target and pairwise prime spacing at least t/(32p²), the singular-box order (0,1,2,4,6,5,3,7) and its reverse satisfy |det E(C)| ≥ a³ exp(-4a)/(2¹⁶p⁶). Forward and inverse singular-value, periodic-alias and factor-rounding errors are explicitly billed. At p≥4096, ceil(233+42 log₂ p) additional bits suffice.
- **All orders under narrower prime placement:** for p≥2²⁰, common t≥p⁷² and one source prime in each of the three specified target-ratio intervals centered at (33,47,62)/64, all 40,320 orders retain a common determinant margin D=2⁻¹⁸ exp(-8a). The rounded forward displacement has σ_min≥2⁻²²D and the exact rounded tensor inverse has σ_min≥2⁻⁵⁰D. ceil(379+72 log₂ p) fractional bits suffice. This is *not* a claim for arbitrary separated triples.

Prime existence is established only with the explicit finite fixtures and qualified eventual argument based on Trudgian's prime-count theorem. No production routine for the actual rounded coefficients is silently admitted.

other_new_prs.title: Forward Gaussian rounding: parity-flux obstruction below half slack
other_new_prs.body:
## Result

Any total injective error-one Hadamard/Gaussian rounder with forward
radial slack below one half must change infinitely many inputs whose
ideal images are already integral. The proof gives a quantitative bound:
at slack at most 3/10, at least \(8m\) even-sum inputs of norm at most
\(4m+2\) must change, for every \(m\geq0\).

In exact half-grid coordinates, an odd-width cube has equal input/output
color counts but eight inaccessible output corners. Each parity-changing
exit forces a nearby exact-valued input to change. If \(K_N\) counts
these changes by transformed output cube, the result is

\[
K_{N+2}-K_{N-2}\geq8
\quad\text{when}\quad
\delta<N-\sqrt{N^2-N+1}.
\]

The parity-preserving subclass consequently has forward optimum one half,
using #7569's credited upper construction. Surjectivity, exact sums,
phase covariance and period identities are not premises of the new
lower theorem.

## Why this helps

#7651 already attains the unrestricted finite threshold through radius
24. This contribution identifies what any all-lattice extension must
change: a finite repair of exact-valued inputs cannot suffice. It does
not claim the unrestricted optimum or repeat larger finite-radius work.
#7696 and #7714/#7743 concern additional exact-sum and iterate contracts.

## Checks and limitations

Run:

    python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-forward-parity-flux

The exact checks cover 2,401 coordinate inputs, four complete cube graphs,
49,664 two-edge choices, equality/escape controls, 9,600 rational cutoffs,
and a separately verified 3,121-input unrestricted finite matching.
Holding its even inputs exact gives only 3,113 matches, with an explicit
321-input/313-neighbor Hall witness certifying the upper bound separately
from the search. Collision and nonlocal-edge mutations reject. The
universal statement rests on the written proof, not finite exhaustion.

No selected caller, physical tariff, positive-density claim or
unrestricted all-lattice construction is supplied. All five foundational
assumptions remain; there is no new kappa.

## Sources and credit

Base: e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. Exact predecessor heads,
scope, proof, receipt and remaining questions are in the package.
Prepared for Jerry Chen / @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance.
Credit #7569 for the half-grid coordinates and upper construction,
#7571 and Nick Petalas's #7651 for the finite Hall problem, Ali Romman's
#6509 for the Gaussian pair, and #6619/#2589 for the radial-obstruction
lineage. Model-assisted review is not human or formal-kernel acceptance.

other_new_prs.title: Prove the exact threshold for fusing two congruent products
other_new_prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

When can a parent obtain the low m bits of two products' sum, including its incoming carry, from one multiplication? If the siblings agree on a low bits on the left and b on the right, the exact threshold is **a+b ≥ m+1** in the direct-product model, even with arbitrary separate encoders and one-sided additive corrections. One bit below the threshold, a single AND of difference parities repairs the high bit. For independent odd pairs, the high-bit-only carryless channel model needs exactly **2m−2 input coordinates per side**.

At m=8 and a=b=4, the two-product control uses 170 AND and 170 XOR gates. The corrected circuit uses **91 AND and 107 XOR**, including the incoming carry. Its clean reversible translation uses 182 Toffoli and 436 CNOT gates. I request review of these bounds, the circuits and their caller applicability. The κ target of 0.003884928046155 remains open.

## Task and overlap

Changed scope on the supplier-boundary-audit card, based on canonical main e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. [Single-product predecessor #7838](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7838) has a different observable. [Gaussian source #7834](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7834) has genuine sum-only parents. [Mixed-rank reference #7830](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7830) retains separate outputs. Exact heads, complete reference histograms, source links and reproduction commands are in the package.

## Validation

The primary verifier checked 1,044,944 admissible residues through five bits, all 65,536 four-bit circuit inputs with carry, and the literal six-bit odd row classes. Independent replay checked both clean gate programs and 20,480 additional eight-bit cases. A complete 20-by-19-bit Gaussian product retained its coefficients, residual, bits and cleanup with 74,655 → 62,284 ordinary word-product dispatches using a width-preserving three-product control. A separate phase control reduced an emitted middle fixture from 1,728 to 1,664 scalar calls. Both are counts of ordinary work. The 145-bit complete replay reached its CPU limit. The separate 8,200-bit diagnostic substituted an exact integer at the wide-worker boundary.

~~~sh
python3 -I -B research/recursive-dot-carry/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/recursive-dot-carry
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/recursive-dot-carry
~~~

## Credit

Clear1nsight, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Separate workers traced the two callers and independently checked the proofs, circuits and source replays. The optional Gaussian control uses the classical three-product identity. Credit for the underlying Gaussian program belongs to aliromman and its cited suppliers. The original mixed-rank and single-product contributors are credited in the package.

## Open next questions

Find a charged parent where the sibling congruence holds on every allowed input. Pin both first consumers and charge retention or reconstruction of any separately observed difference. The current signed deficits are at least 4.88039108995 rational and 1.92561529070 binary units; the ordinary savings here supply zero on those invoices.

other_new_prs.title: Prove sharp carryless channel widths for an ordinary product bit
other_new_prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For separate encodings of two m-bit operands, recover bit m−1 of the ordinary integer product from binary polynomial products. The package proves the exact full-domain GF(2) matrix rank, floor(2^(m−1)/3) + floor(3m/2) − 1 for m ≥ 2. With odd operands, the exact input width per side falls from 2^(m−3)+1 for affine decoding to m−1 for nonlinear decoding. Asking for the next lower bit as well raises the minimum to m. A single jointly mixed width-(m+1) channel produces the full odd product modulo 2^m with an exponential lookup.

The explicit five-bit circuit attains width four with 18 AND and 35 XOR gates in total. Three decoder ANDs are necessary for its fixed encoding. The paper also gives matching all-position bounds for separated convolution digits. These quantities concern an interface to integer multiplication. The independently verified full-multiplier comparator from #7830 is 0.00387992803556; the target of 0.003884928046155 remains open. Claimed κ gain for this package is zero.

## Task and overlap

Base e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. Changed scope from the supplier-boundary-audit card to a separately encoded carryless front end. #6252 bounds the size of propagated carries, #6552 supplies finite-field slices, and #7834 computes a different Gaussian multiplication pipeline. This package derives a product-bit matrix rank and matching channel widths. The #7830 comparator is pinned at 87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15.

## Validation and review requested

Run `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/carryless-middle-bit-rank` from the repository root with Python 3.12 on Linux. The checker covers the literal full and odd rank tables through m=12, 2,867,152 pre-carry digit comparisons, exhaustive five-bit gates, and 349,520 odd-input pairs for each of two field constructions through m=10. A separately written checker excluded every two-AND decoder for the five-bit encoding. Please review the valuation-zero elimination and the distinction between per-side width and actual gate cost.

## Credit and next question

Thathachar's 1997 work on ordered representations and Bryant's earlier work are antecedents for exponential rank arguments about middle-bit multiplication. Clear1nsight used OpenAI Codex for derivation, implementation, and independent agent review. Source pins, proof assumptions and reproducible controls are in the package.

For six-bit odd operands, can one width-six carryless product recover bits four and five together with a small table-free decoder? The exact width lower bound is six. The seven-coordinate field construction gives a control. A proposed width-six code can first be checked for conflicting returns on all 1,024 input pairs.
